column1: # rowkeydb's own build lines, which scripts/check.sh allows for a consumer on
# v0.9.0 or later: every option line of .bazelrc after the import of the
# shared options, every override, patch and declaration of a shared module
# in MODULE.bazel, and every copts, features and defines of a BUILD file.
# Each entry is a kind (bazelrc, module or build), the line as check.sh
# prints it, and the reason the consumer needs it, separated by tabs. A
# line is added here before the consumer adds it, and removed after.

column3: RocksDB throws in multi_scan, memtable, string_util, write_prepared_txn_db, backup_engine and options_helper; an exception reaching -fno-exceptions code terminates.
jemalloc's C++ operator new catches std::bad_alloc to honour the throwing and non-throwing new contract.
RocksDB's transaction code asserts with dynamic_cast wherever NDEBUG is undefined (the default and sanitizer builds).
jemalloc is the process-wide allocator of every rowkeydb binary and test, its own code's and every statically linked dependency's allocations.
jemalloc's run-time tuning baked into the binary, so that it needs no MALLOC_CONF in the deployment.
jemalloc's heap profiler, dormant unless MALLOC_CONF turns it on, for on-demand heap profiles of the shipped binary.
The sanitizers replace the allocator to instrument it, so no sanitizer build links jemalloc.
RocksDB loads unaligned data on purpose.
rowkeydb exports its metrics through the OpenTelemetry C++ SDK, whose gauges need ABI version 2.

Reports a recyclable record type in a log that is not recycled before its length is trusted, so that such a type never silently ends the log.
Stops the recovery of the logs and the manifest at a log's first damaged record; a record torn by a power loss ends the log without failing the durable mode's startup.
